vo.text: This stone was once a dinosaur's bone.
How does a dinosaur bone turn into stone?
Long ago, a big, gentle dinosaur lived right here, munching ferns by the river.
One day, very old and tired, it lay down and died.
The river brought mud and sand, which covered its bones like a blanket.
More mud came. And more. Layer on layer, for millions of years.
Deep down, water seeped into the bones and left tiny bits of stone. Slowly, they turned to rock.
Then wind and rain slowly wore the land away.
One sunny day, a girl with a brush spotted something poking out of the rock.
A fossil! A real dinosaur bone, turned to stone.
I wonder what is waiting under your feet.
